analysis: Steroids are commonly used as adjunctive therapy in certain forms of tuberculosis to reduce inflammation and prevent complications. They are indicated in tuberculous meningitis to reduce cerebral edema and in tuberculous pericarditis to prevent constrictive pericarditis. In cases of adrenal involvement, steroids may be necessary to replace deficient adrenal hormones. However, in ileo-caecal tuberculosis, steroids are not typically indicated as part of the treatment regimen, which primarily involves anti-tubercular drugs.
